svg.text: Spinal motor pools are ordered, overlapping, and longitudinal
Broad topography, convergent input, and spinal interconnections coordinate many muscles at once.
Broad organization within a limb enlargement
Medial-to-lateral order is graded and overlapping, not a set of isolated muscle buttons.
Direct and indirect input converge on neighboring motor pools
A pool is defined by its target muscle, although neighboring territories and inputs can overlap.
Spinal interneurons distribute and reshape much sensory and descending input
Shared input does not eliminate differential recruitment within or between motor pools
Motor pools extend across segments and interact across both sides
An action recruits distributed pools rather than one muscle, one segment, or one side of the cord.
Schematic distributions: pool ends fade across segment boundaries, and actual segmental ranges overlap and vary.
Spinal interneurons coordinate pools within a segment, across segments, and across the midline.
Spinal anatomy creates useful biases without dividing movement into isolated muscles, segments, or pathways.
